learning_outcomes.text: Can geometrically describe movements that occur in nature and technology within the framework of kinematics.
Are able to transfer technical systems into a mathematical model.
Can represent physical vectors in different coordinate systems.
Know the concept of generalized coordinates.
Are able to make the choice of generalized coordinates.
Understand the decomposition of general rigid body movements into translational and rotational movements.
Understand the relationship between forces and movements.
Can consider standard joints in the form of constraint equations.
Know the most important principles of technical mechanics.
Are able to apply the cutting method.
Can apply the force theorem and the moment theorem.
Master D'Alembert's principle (formal reduction of kinetics to statics).
Know how to evaluate the fundamental dynamic law in different coordinate systems.
Know how to apply the energy theorem to single bodies and multi-body systems.
Know the associated areas of validity for the energy theorem.
Master different methods for setting up the equations of motion for particle systems and rigid body systems.

syllabus_topics: Work and Energy Theorem for Multi-body Systems
